why: The C5 rewrite intended to allow cuts at light function words while keeping verbs with core arguments, but the model instead shifted many cuts inward, fragmenting noun phrases, enumerations and verb+modifier sequences (e.g. splitting “did not walk upright” and breaking “Scottish justice” into separate pieces). That produced tiny gains on very short pieces but net harm in mid-length bins (≤5 and ≤10) — 177 (worse) vs 144 (better) — so overall H_set fell slightly.
lesson: When revising predicate/NP guidance, avoid wording that implicitly encourages cutting apart heads or fragmenting short/mid-length units; preserve verb‑argument and NP integrity so cuts don't create many small fragments (especially in the ≤5–≤10 word range).
